decisions: The calculation logic must live in src/split.ts and the UI must consume that module.
Use integer cents in the pure calculation so exact-sum behavior can be guaranteed.
Deterministic remainder distribution is implemented with the largest-remainder method and ascending index as the tiebreaker.
toCents collapses to 12 significant digits before rounding, so a decimal .5 tie such as 1.005 rounds away from zero instead of being pulled down by binary representation error.
concerns: Need executable evidence that splitBill behaves correctly in the required scenarios, not just that the implementation looks plausible.
Weight quantisation at 1e-6 precision may collapse extremely small differences between weights; watch whether tests or UI requirements expose that as a problem.
Need verification that both npm test and npm run build pass without errors.
last_instruction: Replace src/split.test.ts with a full Vitest suite for the split module that covers the brief end-to-end: even split, weighted split, tax+tip, and at least one awkward-fraction case proving the shares sum exactly to totalCents with deterministic remainder distribution. Use npm test to confirm the suite passes, then report the branch diff, the full contents of src/split.test.ts, and the npm test output.
